bib.title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v3, 22 May 2024, marked 'Preprint. Under review.')

read.skipped: Reference list (chars ~37,400-69,300) skimmed only for lineage; figures 3-11 are plots, only captions read.

question: Can finetuning a small number of learned interventions on hidden representations of a frozen LM match or beat weight-based PEFTs such as LoRA with far fewer trainable parameters?
hypothesis: Representations encode rich semantic information, so editing representations might be a more powerful alternative to weight updates.
contributions: Define the ReFT family of methods that learn task-specific interventions on hidden representations of a frozen base model
Define LoReFT (low-rank linear subspace ReFT, built on distributed interchange interventions) and DiReFT, an ablation that trades some performance for efficiency
Evaluate on commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction-following and GLUE against PEFTs, tuning on dev sets only

method.summary: A frozen LM gets interventions Phi(h) = h + R^T(Wh + b - Rh) (LoReFT) applied at p prefix and s suffix token positions in a chosen set of layers; only R (orthonormal rows, rank r), W and b are trained with the LM cross-entropy loss. DiReFT drops the orthogonality constraint and the subtraction. Baselines are mostly copied from earlier papers.
method.task: parameter-efficient finetuning for commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, instruction following, and GLUE classification

other.note: scores copied from Hu et al. 2023, Liu et al. 2024c (DoRA), Wu et al. 2024a (RED), Li et al. 2023, Kopiczko et al. 2024; not rerun

training.objective: Cross-entropy with teacher forcing over output positions (generation); cross-entropy on a classification head over the first-token (CLS) representation for GLUE
training.lr: searched, per Tables 5-8: {9e-5 ... 3e-3} for LLaMA GSM8K; 9e-4 fixed for Alpaca-52K; {1e-4 ... 3e-3} for GLUE. Chosen LLaMA values are underlined in the PDF and lost in the text; GLUE chosen values in Tables 9-12 (e.g. 6e-4 for MNLI)
training.warmup: warmup ratio searched in {0, 0.06, 0.10} (LLaMA GSM8K), 0.00 (Alpaca), {0 ... 0.2} (GLUE); chosen values per Tables 9-12
training.batch_size: searched {4, 8, 16, 32, 64} (GSM8K), {16, 32, 64, 128} (Alpaca, GLUE); GLUE chosen 32 (8 for DiReFT RoBERTa-base RTE)
training.epochs: 6 (commonsense), 12 (arithmetic) chosen; GLUE 20-60 per task; Alpaca search {1, 3, 6, 9, 12}; 3-epoch reruns in Tables 14-15
training.hardware: single GPU: NVIDIA A100 40G/80G or RTX 6000
training.wall_clock: 18 minutes to train Llama-2 Chat 7B on 1K examples on one A100 40G (Table 3 footnote); under 10 minutes for the multi-task demo; 30 seconds for the 5-example demo
training.seeds: 3 seeds (commonsense, arithmetic), 2 seeds (instruction tuning), 5 seeds (GLUE: 42 for tuning, plus 43-46); some RTE, CoLA and QQP seeds replaced or best-of-3

other.intervention_hyperparameters: prefix positions p, suffix positions s, layer set L, tied or untied weights across positions, rank r
other.GLUE_settings: rank 1, all layers, untied, per-task position p (p1 to p11, see Tables 9-12), tuned separately for LoReFT and DiReFT
other.dev_sets: hyperparameters tuned on dev sets that do not overlap the test sets; the LLaMA-7B GSM8K setting is reused for commonsense (6 epochs) and for 13B, 'without additional tuning'
other.chosen_values_not_in_text: the best LLaMA settings were marked by underline and are not recoverable from the extracted text

inference.decoding: greedy without sampling for commonsense; Hu et al. 2023 decoding for arithmetic; greedy with repetition penalty for instruction tuning
inference.max_tokens: 32 new tokens (commonsense, arithmetic); 2048 new tokens (instruction tuning)
inference.samples: 1 generation per item; scores averaged over 3 (commonsense, arithmetic), 2 (instruction), 5 (GLUE) training seeds
inference.prompting: Hu et al. 2023 template with string normalisation (commonsense, arithmetic); Taori et al. 2023 Alpaca template (instruction)

parameters.beam_search: arithmetic uses beam-search-like Hu et al. settings; text gives temperature 0.3 only

limits: Authors: mainly the LLaMA family explored for lack of resources; no other families or vision-language models.
Authors: the large hyperparameter search space is not fully explored; automating the search is future work.
Authors: arithmetic reasoning is weaker; they suggest chain-of-thought length dilutes a fixed-position intervention, and say no method wins across all four tasks.
Authors: how ReFT works is not explained; memorisation experiments are early and use untuned hyperparameters.
ReFT needs hooks in the computation graph, so it cannot be merged into weights as LoRA can; it adds inference overhead (Appendix H).
Baseline numbers are copied from other papers with different tuning protocols; LoReFT uses more epochs than LoRA/DoRA (checked in Appendix D.3 only for commonsense and arithmetic).
Llama-3 8B was run only on commonsense; instruction tuning is judged by GPT-4 win-rate on one 7B model with 2 seeds.
Not an RL paper: no reward, policy or RL objective; training is supervised cross-entropy.
Chosen LLaMA hyperparameters are underlined in the PDF and not recoverable from the text; step counts, FLOPs and total GPU hours are not stated.

terms.definition: A set of f interventions I = {I1,...,If}; for two interventions on the same layer, positions must be disjoint and parameters independent.
A tuple <Phi, P, l> of an intervention function, a set of input positions, and a layer.
Phi(h) = h + R^T(Wh + b - Rh), editing the representation in the r-dimensional subspace spanned by rows of R.
Phi(h) = h + W2^T(W1h + b), LoReFT without the orthogonality constraint and the difference operation.
